intro: Electricians troubleshoot, repair and check quality every day, and those skills carry into many trades. The closest of the 25 careers below is Electrical Power-Line Installers and Repairers, with an 82% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $95,320, which is 51% more than electricians earn.
why_it_works: Tracing a fault through a panel takes the same thinking as fixing a motor, a transit system or an elevator. O*NET rates troubleshooting at 4 out of 5 for electricians, one of the highest skill scores on any trade page. All 25 matches need no more education than you already have. What changes is the equipment: you may need to learn new machines, read control software and handle more customer negotiation.
tips: List the voltages, systems and codes you have worked with; specific equipment matters more than general experience.
Look at elevator work: Elevator and Escalator Installers and Repairers earn $109,910, 74% more than the $63,190 electrician median.
Ask utilities about line apprenticeships, which pay while you train for power-line work.

faq.q: What jobs can former electricians do?
faq.a: The closest matches are power-line installers (82%), electric motor and power tool repairers (81%) and transportation equipment electricians (75%), based on O*NET 31.0. HVAC mechanics are also close at 74%, with a median of $61,010, which is 3% less than electricians earn.

faq.q: Which careers for electricians pay more?
faq.a: 16 of the 25 matches pay more than the $63,190 electrician median. Elevator installers earn $109,910 (74% more), Ship Engineers $109,530 (73% more) and powerhouse and substation repairers $103,020 (63% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Most of these jobs also pay during training.

faq.q: Do electricians need more schooling to change trades?
faq.a: No. All 25 matches usually need no more education than an electrician already has. Half of the workers in the closest match have a high school diploma (50%), and 39% hold a post-secondary certificate, so on-the-job training and licenses matter most.

faq.q: What new skills do electricians need for other trades?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are equipment maintenance, programming, operations monitoring and negotiation. Repairing already rates 3.5 out of 5 for your job in O*NET, so learning a new type of equipment is usually the main step.
